title: Putin announces suspension of Russia's participation in the New START treaty
body:
On 21 February 2023, in his annual state-of-the-nation address, Russian President Vladimir Putin announced that Russia was suspending its participation in the New START treaty, the last remaining major nuclear arms control agreement between Russia and the United States. He stressed that Russia was suspending its obligations rather than fully withdrawing.

The treaty was signed in 2010 by Barack Obama and Dmitry Medvedev. It limits each side to 1,550 deployed nuclear warheads and 700 deployed missiles and bombers, and provides for on-site inspections. It was extended by five years in early 2021, days before it was due to expire. Mutual inspections had been suspended since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, and Moscow had refused in autumn 2022 to allow them to resume.

Putin said the United States and its NATO allies had openly stated a goal of inflicting "strategic defeat" on Russia. He said Russia should be ready to resume nuclear testing if the United States did so, though Russia would not be first to test. He also argued that British and French nuclear arsenals must be taken into account before any return to talks. The U.S. State Department said Russia's refusal to allow inspections threatened arms control. NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg expressed regret and urged Russia to reconsider.
